question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Category III AIF, is launching a close-ended scheme with a targeted corpus of INR 150 crore. As per Regulation 10 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, what is the minimum continuing interest (sponsor commitment) that the Sponsor or Manager must maintain in the scheme?

answer.text: INR 7.5 crore (the lower of 5% of INR 150 cr = INR 7.5 cr or INR 10 cr)
INR 10 crore (the lower of 5% of INR 150 cr = INR 7.5 cr or INR 10 cr)
INR 5 crore (2.5% of corpus or INR 5 cr, whichever is lower)

explanation.text: The Logic: For a Category III AIF, the Sponsor/Manager continuing interest is 5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is LOWER. 5% of INR 150 cr = INR 7.5 cr; compared to INR 10 cr, the lower is INR 7.5 crore. The commitment must be in the form of actual investment in the scheme (not a waiver of management fee) and cannot be reduced after First Close. The Trap: Option B picks INR 10 cr by reading "whichever higher" instead of lower. Option C (3.75 cr) is 2.5% — a Cat I/II rule, wrong category. Option D uses the Cat I/II cap of INR 5 cr — swapped category. Note: When corpus * 5% exceeds INR 10 cr (corpus > INR 200 cr), the INR 10 cr cap binds. For schemes below INR 200 cr corpus, the 5% figure governs.
